solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Instrument that's initially good for Parisians in foreign capital

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word that's
in puts the French word inside the name of the capital city

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy, foreign to a British setter
bon is the French word for good

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is described through a French word for good, picked up in some foreign city.
explanation.definitionFit: A trombone is a brass instrument with a sliding tube.

clue.text: Plant without root's outside under bone

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the following letters below the bone

parts.note: a rib is a bone of the chest
w/o is the written abbreviation for without

indicators.note: outside asks for the outer letters only of the word root

explanation.surface: A plant is described as lacking the outer part of its root and sitting below a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is not an instruction to remove anything: it supplies W/O, its written short form.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribwort is a plantain, a common weed of lawns and verges.

clue.text: Historian in press register digesting English verse

indicators.note: digesting means taking something in, so the press word swallows the other letters

parts.note: the press is part of the media
a register is a list

explanation.surface: A historian appears in the newspapers' records, chewing over some English poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A medievalist is a scholar of the Middle Ages, so a kind of historian.

clue.text: Hunter about to imbibe port

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so the word for about takes in the port

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A hunter is about to have a drink of port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink but is the city of Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is the hunter of Greek myth, also a constellation.

clue.text: Monstrosity has detective angry

parts.note: a private eye is a detective
sore means angry, chiefly in American usage

explanation.surface: Something ugly has made a detective cross.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is an ugly building or sight, a monstrosity.

clue.text: Do well with riveting? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely tells us the answer is part of the words with riveting, running across them

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether riveting counts as doing well, then admits it does not quite.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive is to flourish or prosper.

clue.text: Old sycophant, one taking courses with demon driver?

parts.note: Mr Toad in The Wind in the Willows is a reckless motorist
an eater is one who takes courses of a meal

explanation.surface: A student taking courses alongside a reckless motorist is the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' suggests education but means courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A toadeater, the origin of toady, is a dated term for a fawning flatterer.

clue.text: Game finally given outdoor enclosure

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word given

explanation.surface: A game is finally given an enclosure to play in outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A run is an enclosed area for animals, as in a chicken run.

clue.text: Gallery about to be erected in museum

indicators.note: in puts the turned word inside the museum

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means set upright, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A gallery is about to be put up in a museum.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed gallery or porch along a house's outside.

clue.text: Useful gift for doctor having fish in county estate, we're told

parts.note: Beds is the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county
the ide is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: we're told means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a manor is a landed estate

explanation.surface: A doctor's useful gift is a fish living in a country estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A good bedside manner is a doctor's way with patients, a valuable talent.

clue.text: Control deliveries in centre of Bognor

indicators.note: in puts the cricket word between the central letters
centre of asks for the middle two letters of Bognor

parts.note: Bognor Regis is an English seaside town
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries

explanation.surface: Someone controls the deliveries in the middle of Bognor, the seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern is to rule or have control over.

clue.text: Plain individual, but partial

definitions.note: a noun here, a component tone of a sound

parts.note: overt means plain, open to view
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: Someone is a plain individual but biased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partial' reads as biased, but here it is the acoustics noun for one component of a note.
explanation.definitionFit: In acoustics an overtone is a partial, a higher frequency sounding above the fundamental.

clue.text: Irritable lady gutted about charge, needing physical contact?

parts.note: touchy means easily irritated
a fee is a charge; about is read loosely, the charge sitting beside the remains of the lady

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters of lady

explanation.surface: An irritable woman, gutted about a charge, needs a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' does no precise work: the charge simply sits before the L and Y left by 'gutted', so 'about' is best read as loose positioning.
explanation.definitionFit: Touchy-feely describes someone keen on hugging and open emotional display.

clue.text: Son educates parent finally about minute part of engine

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters go round the abbreviation for minute

parts.note: to educate is to teach

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word parent

explanation.surface: A son educates his parent, at last, about a small part of an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam chest is the chamber that feeds steam to the cylinder in a steam engine.

clue.text: Unreproducible chit Porgy composed

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters of chit Porgy are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gershwin's Porgy and Bess is protected; this score note cannot be copied.
explanation.definitionFit: Copyright as an adjective means protected by copyright, so not legally reproducible.

clue.text: US state uniform and headgear making comeback

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the word for headgear is read backwards

parts.note: a hat is headgear

explanation.surface: In a US state, uniforms and hats are back in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is a western American state.

clue.text: Princess, one travelling east in Gulf State

indicators.note: in an across answer east is rightward, so the letter for one moves to the end

parts.note: Iran borders the Persian Gulf
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A princess goes east within a Gulf country.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is an Indian queen or princess, wife of a raja.

clue.text: Like certain exercises with a crashing bore in charge

indicators.note: crashing means smashed up, so the letters of bore are scrambled

explanation.surface: Some exercises come with a crashing bore running things.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobic exercise is the sustained kind that raises breathing and heart rate.

clue.text: He appears confused at first adapting old crosscountry event

indicators.note: adapting means altering, so the pooled letters are rearranged
at first asks for only the opening letter of the word confused

explanation.surface: He seems puzzled at first by changes to an old cross-country race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' looks like the anagram signal but only gives its C; 'adapting' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper chase is hare and hounds, a run following a trail of paper scraps.

clue.text: Pair consuming coffee and course of meal

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the pair's letters swallow the coffee

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: Two people drink coffee and have a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A platter, such as a seafood platter, is a dish served as a course.

clue.text: Extra place by ancient city in South America

indicators.note: in puts the city and place inside the south and America letters

parts.note: US is the United States, America
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: An extra spot beside an ancient city somewhere in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South America' looks like one place but is S and US, split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus is an amount left over, more than is needed.

clue.text: Standards of service right for inclusion by agents

indicators.note: for inclusion by means taken in by, so the agents enclose the other letters

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency, a body of agents
a rite is a religious service

explanation.surface: Standards of service are right for agents to adopt.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are principles or standards by which something is judged.

clue.text: Maintain a fine business

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, on pencils
a firm is a business

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a business is going well.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to affirm it, assert it as true.

clue.text: Bikini, possibly, demanding a tax

parts.note: a toll is a tax or charge, as on a road

explanation.surface: A bikini costs a lot, demanding a tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bikini' is not swimwear but Bikini Atoll in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini is a Pacific coral atoll, a ring-shaped reef, used for nuclear tests.

clue.text: As loose dogs may be, or doctors driven to patients, do we hear?

indicators.note: do we hear signals the words are heard, not spelt

parts.note: doctors taken to patients are brought there to heal them

explanation.surface: A question about stray dogs and doctors being ferried to their patients.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog brought to heel is made to walk at its owner's side, under control.

clue.text: Work hard, sacrificing time for painting

indicators.note: sacrificing means giving up, so the letter for time is dropped

parts.note: to toil is to work hard

explanation.surface: Someone works hard, giving up time for painting.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil is a painting done in oil paints.

clue.text: Leader of Oxford Group keeping church cat

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the church letters go within
leader of asks for the first letter of Oxford

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The head of an Oxford group keeps a church cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a wild spotted cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Motor sport competitor's friend is right outside

indicators.note: outside means the letters for right wrap round the others

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A rally driver's friend is outside on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A rallyist is someone who takes part in motor rallies.
